## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the handling of `limit=0` so callers can request all orders as issue #12 specifies.

## Changes

The pull request adds an optional limit to the newest-first order listing. It introduces a pagination helper that supports offsets and rejects negative limits and offsets.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/orders.py:9 — correctness — Treat a zero order limit as unlimited — `list_orders(orders, limit=0)` returns an empty list when orders exist. Issue #12 defines zero as unlimited, but passing it to `paginate` sets the slice’s stop index to zero. — Order views that use zero to request the full history display no orders. — Fix: Convert zero to `None` before calling `paginate` and extend `test_newest_first` to cover the zero-limit call.

## Suggestions

- app/paging.py:13 — tests — Cover the first page after the last item — `paginate([1, 2], limit=2, offset=2)` should return an empty page, but neither pagination test that uses an offset passes one equal to the item count. — The suite would miss a regression that returns a nonempty page after a caller consumes an exact multiple of the page size.
